- Strong share of business in the OE segment, with capabilities upgraded to stay technologically relevant in each segment
- Pre-positioning of materials and coatings has resulted in increased engagement on new OEM platforms, and supplies to OEM customers under the new emission norms commenced from last year
- Technology in place to cater to blended gasoline and multi-fuel options being suggested by the Government, alongside continued ICE and hybrid platform development
- Development of lead free high strength materials has opened markets with customers seeking indigenous solutions
- Consolidation of all core-product operations into the Hosur plant, giving economies of scale and better cost control at one location
- 20% joint venture with Daido Metal Company Ltd., Japan (BBL Daido Private Limited), described as giving satisfactory returns on the investments made
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price inflation and shortage of critical inputs — The last quarter of the year witnessed high price increases in all inputs - steel, non-ferrous metals, petroleum products and gases - due to the geo-political conflict in the Middle East; availability was also a serious issue which posed challenges in fulfilling commitments to customers, and management states the challenges continue to exist with higher levels of prices and shortages of critical inputs.
- Dependence on Tier 1 suppliers rather than direct OEM supply — Products like bushings have become more for supply into Tier 1 suppliers than to OEMs directly. The AR calls this both an advantage and a disadvantage, and states explicitly that on the negative side there are business risks associated with such opportunities.
- Global warranty exposure in the export / global supply chain — While quality, delivery and price have to be competitive, the AR flags that the important requirement of Global warranty needs to be studied in the background of the warranty clauses provided by the OEMs - a liability tail on parts exported to plants outside the country.
- Electrification of the vehicle fleet eroding the ICE-linked core product base — Electric motive power in relation to replacement of IC engines has gained traction in the two wheeler, three wheeler and passenger car segments and inter-city EV travel has gained acceptance; the Company notes ICE sales growth relative to EV is still significant and says it will continue investment in its core products albeit cautiously, which frames the pace of the EV shift as the key structural uncertainty.
- Technology / emission-norm obsolescence in core products — New generations of vehicles conforming to stringent emission norms call for bearings with matching characteristics, and multi-fuel and blended-gasoline options are being explored by OEMs; staying on new platforms depends on continuously pre-positioning materials, coatings and processes.
- Execution risk in the new EV battery-pack and Engineering and Projects ventures — The battery-pack manufacturing facility is still under installation, trials are ongoing and only initial orders for battery packs and BMS have been received, while the Engineering and Projects segment is new and its revenue is recognised stage-wise - so both revenue streams are unproven.
- Concentration of all core-product manufacturing at a single location — Operations of all core products were consolidated into the Hosur plant last year. The AR presents this as a source of economies of scale and cost control, but it means core output now depends on one site.
- Outstanding statutory transfer flagged by the Secretarial Auditor — The Secretarial Audit Report qualifies its compliance opinion, stating the Company is yet to transfer the shares becoming due for transfer to the demat account of the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority and to file the necessary e-forms; the Directors' Report says the transfer is in process.

outlook.body:
- Consolidate the operations of all core products into the Hosur plant to gain economies of scale and better cost control at one location
- Continue investing cautiously in core bearing products, backed by new ICE and hybrid platform development, while positioning materials and coatings for stringent emission norms
- Enter the EV business with manufacture and supply of battery pack power systems, assembling packs with BMS in-house and converting trials into commercial supply
- Build the alloy-powder business by developing customers in the sintering, brazing, filter and printing industries and by pursuing export markets for powders

outlook.body: The main structural step was the consolidation of the operations of all core products into the Hosur plant, completed last year, which management expects to give economies of scale and better cost control at one location; plant utilisation was described as good throughout the year. The new powder facility has been in operation for the last two years, and customer development in the sintering, brazing, filter and printing industries has progressed aggressively, with export markets for powders also being pursued. The Company proposes to enter the EV business with manufacture and supply of battery pack power systems: that manufacturing facility is under installation, trials are being conducted for packs assembled in-house with the addition of BMS, discussions with potential customers for commercial supply have commenced, and initial orders for battery packs and BMS have been received. During the year the Company also entered a new Engineering and Projects segment catering to equipment design and manufacture. No rupee capex quantum, project cost or commissioning date is stated in the routed text.

outlook.body:
- Demand for products used in Heavy Vehicles, Tractors, Powders and Strips is expected to offer good opportunities, coupled with the cost control measures undertaken
- The outlook for the current year is positive with other product segments also projected to show growth to add to the core business
- Stringent emission norms require bearings with matching characteristics, and pre-positioned materials and coatings have increased engagement on new OEM platforms
- Growth in sales of ICE vehicles relative to EVs remains significant, and new ICE and hybrid platform development supports continued investment in core products
- Government push on fuel blending, with fuel additives having reached a level of 20% of ethanol in petroleum products, plus multi-fuel options being explored by OEMs, which the Company is technologically positioned to serve
- Alignment of Indian emission standards with global standards, and global sourcing offices set up in India, open export supply-chain opportunities
- Product assemblies aggregating at Tier 1 suppliers means bushings increasingly go to Tier 1s rather than OEMs directly, an advantage through their global business but with associated business risk and global warranty clauses to be studied
- Industry volumes grew across all segments during the year, aided by GST reduction, with passenger vehicles up 7.9%, two wheelers 10.7% (scooters alone 18.5%) and commercial vehicles 12.6%
- Input cost and availability are a headwind: the last quarter saw high price increases in steel, non-ferrous metals, petroleum products and gases due to the geo-political conflict in the Middle East, with shortages of critical inputs continuing
- Initial orders have been received from customers for Battery packs and BMS, with trials being conducted for packs assembled in the Company along with addition of BMS
- The new Engineering and Projects segment added to revenue during the year by virtue of stage wise recognition

capital_allocation.body:
- Consolidate the operations of all core products into the Hosur plant to gain economies of scale and better cost control at one location
- Continue investing cautiously in core bearing products, backed by new ICE and hybrid platform development, while positioning materials and coatings for stringent emission norms
- Enter the EV business with manufacture and supply of battery pack power systems, assembling packs with BMS in-house and converting trials into commercial supply
- Build the alloy-powder business by developing customers in the sintering, brazing, filter and printing industries and by pursuing export markets for powders
- Engage with Tier 1 suppliers and with global sourcing offices set up in India to become part of the supply chain exporting parts to plants outside the country
- Develop lead free high strength materials to serve customers seeking indigenous solutions
- Upgrade technology, reduce costs and provide integrated solutions across the OE, After Market and Export segments
- Grow the newly entered Engineering and Projects segment covering equipment design and manufacture

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The main structural step was the consolidation of the operations of all core products into the Hosur plant, completed last year, which management expects to give economies of scale and better cost control at one location; plant utilisation was described as good throughout the year. The new powder facility has been in operation for the last two years, and customer development in the sintering, brazing, filter and printing industries has progressed aggressively, with export markets for powders also being pursued. The Company proposes to enter the EV business with manufacture and supply of battery pack power systems: that manufacturing facility is under installation, trials are being conducted for packs assembled in-house with the addition of BMS, discussions with potential customers for commercial supply have commenced, and initial orders for battery packs and BMS have been received. During the year the Company also entered a new Engineering and Projects segment catering to equipment design and manufacture. No rupee capex quantum, project cost or commissioning date is stated in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong share of business in the OE segment, with capabilities upgraded to stay technologically relevant in each segment
- Pre-positioning of materials and coatings has resulted in increased engagement on new OEM platforms, and supplies to OEM customers under the new emission norms commenced from last year
- Technology in place to cater to blended gasoline and multi-fuel options being suggested by the Government, alongside continued ICE and hybrid platform development
- Development of lead free high strength materials has opened markets with customers seeking indigenous solutions
- Consolidation of all core-product operations into the Hosur plant, giving economies of scale and better cost control at one location
- 20% joint venture with Daido Metal Company Ltd., Japan (BBL Daido Private Limited), described as giving satisfactory returns on the investments made

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price inflation and shortage of critical inputs — The last quarter of the year witnessed high price increases in all inputs - steel, non-ferrous metals, petroleum products and gases - due to the geo-political conflict in the Middle East; availability was also a serious issue which posed challenges in fulfilling commitments to customers, and management states the challenges continue to exist with higher levels of prices and shortages of critical inputs.
- Dependence on Tier 1 suppliers rather than direct OEM supply — Products like bushings have become more for supply into Tier 1 suppliers than to OEMs directly. The AR calls this both an advantage and a disadvantage, and states explicitly that on the negative side there are business risks associated with such opportunities.
- Global warranty exposure in the export / global supply chain — While quality, delivery and price have to be competitive, the AR flags that the important requirement of Global warranty needs to be studied in the background of the warranty clauses provided by the OEMs - a liability tail on parts exported to plants outside the country.
- Electrification of the vehicle fleet eroding the ICE-linked core product base — Electric motive power in relation to replacement of IC engines has gained traction in the two wheeler, three wheeler and passenger car segments and inter-city EV travel has gained acceptance; the Company notes ICE sales growth relative to EV is still significant and says it will continue investment in its core products albeit cautiously, which frames the pace of the EV shift as the key structural uncertainty.
- Technology / emission-norm obsolescence in core products — New generations of vehicles conforming to stringent emission norms call for bearings with matching characteristics, and multi-fuel and blended-gasoline options are being explored by OEMs; staying on new platforms depends on continuously pre-positioning materials, coatings and processes.
- Execution risk in the new EV battery-pack and Engineering and Projects ventures — The battery-pack manufacturing facility is still under installation, trials are ongoing and only initial orders for battery packs and BMS have been received, while the Engineering and Projects segment is new and its revenue is recognised stage-wise - so both revenue streams are unproven.
- Concentration of all core-product manufacturing at a single location — Operations of all core products were consolidated into the Hosur plant last year. The AR presents this as a source of economies of scale and cost control, but it means core output now depends on one site.
- Outstanding statutory transfer flagged by the Secretarial Auditor — The Secretarial Audit Report qualifies its compliance opinion, stating the Company is yet to transfer the shares becoming due for transfer to the demat account of the Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority and to file the necessary e-forms; the Directors' Report says the transfer is in process.
